title: everyone on the floor, everyone the same meal
hook: everyone on the floor, everyone the same meal

segments.voice: Yesterday: Waheguru. Wahe, wow; guru, the teacher. Today, a meal plenty of people have eaten sitting on a gurdwara floor.

Next to the Golden Temple in Amritsar there's a kitchen that never closes. Anyone can walk in and eat: no ticket, no questions. People at the temple speak of tens of thousands of meals on an ordinary day. And there are no chairs. A banker sits beside a laborer, a first-time visitor beside a grandmother who's come for sixty years, all on the floor in long rows. Where you sit usually says who you are. Here, it can't.
screen: `A KITCHEN THAT NEVER CLOSES.` → `NO TICKET. NO CHAIRS.` → `LONG ROWS ON THE FLOOR.`

segments.voice: Langar is the free community kitchen, and the meal that comes out of it. Gurdwaras keep one. Tradition traces it to Guru Nanak, who shared food with everyone who came to his town of Kartarpur, and the Gurus after him built it into an institution. Here's why it mattered. In Nanak's Punjab, caste rules decided who could eat with whom, and who could even cook for whom. Eating side by side across those lines could be a scandal. The langar did it on purpose, every day. The row everyone sits in even has its own name: pangat. Three details carry the idea. The floor: nobody sits higher, because there's nothing to sit higher on. The food: simple and vegetarian, so someone of any faith or diet can eat without asking what's in it. And the guest list: there isn't one. Any faith, or none. You sit down, hold out your hands, and someone puts a roti in them. The meal is a teaching you can taste: one God, one row.
screen: `LANGAR — THE KITCHEN AND THE MEAL.` · `EATING ACROSS THE LINES OF CASTE.` · `PANGAT — THE ROW.` · `THE FLOOR, THE FOOD, THE GUEST LIST.`

segments.voice: One breath with the bell. Picture yourself in the row: on your left, someone you'd never usually sit beside; on your right, someone else. Breathe in. As you breathe out, hold out your hands, palms up, the way people do when the roti comes down the row.
Langar. The free kitchen, and the meal where everyone sits in one row and eats the same food. Second word.
Your line: nobody sits higher. That's the whole teaching of the meal, in three words. Day two, done.

story.title: dinner on the highway
story.text: Just before Christmas in 2020, France suddenly closed its border with England, and thousands of truck drivers were stranded in Kent, stuck in their cabs for days. Then Sikh volunteers turned up. They had cooked in their gurdwara kitchens, and they walked the lines of trucks, knocking on cab doors and handing up hot meals to drivers from all over Europe. Nobody asked who anyone was. It was langar, served on the side of the road.
story.source: news reports, December 2020: Sikh volunteers and gurdwaras in Kent feeding drivers stranded by the French border closure
